title: papyrus.toml
description: Papyrus project manifest. Relative paths are relative to this file; values may use ${NAME} variables ([var], papyrus.var setting, papyrus_analyzer --var), ${env:NAME} environment variables, ${game:SkyrimSE} game installations from the registry (Windows only), ${workspaceFolder} and a leading ~.

$schema.description: The JSON schema of this file, for editors (e.g. "file://schemas/papyrus.schema.json"). Ignored by papyrus_analyzer.

var.description: Shared defaults of ${NAME} variables; values may use ${env:NAME} for environment variables. Overridden by the papyrus.var editor setting / papyrus_analyzer --var and [var] of papyrus.local.toml. Keep machine specific paths out of this committed file. NAME.workspace = true takes the value of [workspace.var].

path.description: Path of PapyrusCompiler.exe. Without it, the built-in compiler is used.

args.description: Extra arguments passed to the compiler as is.

sources.description: Directories of the scripts to compile, searched recursively.

output.description: Directory of the compiled .pex files; the directory structure of sources is kept. Decompiled scripts go to its decompile folder.

imports.description: Other script source directories, in lookup order (after sources).

flags.description: The flags file, e.g. TESV_Papyrus_Flags.flg. Required by PapyrusCompiler.exe; without it, the built-in compiler uses the flags of Skyrim.

lints.description: Lint levels, as in clippy: by lint (`papyrus_analyzer lint --list`), by group or `all`. A lint wins over its group, which wins over `all`.

workspace.description: Use [workspace.lints] of the workspace, like in Cargo.toml. Without it, that table does not apply. Must be true, and alone in this table.

exclude.description: Scripts without lint problems nor fixes, e.g. ["src/vendor", "**/*_gen.psc"]. Relative to this file; `*` any text of a name, `?` one character, `**` any directories. Without `/` at any depth; a directory leaves out what is below it. Case is ignored.

warnings.description: deny: every warning is an error (like -D warnings).

suspicious.description: Code that is probably wrong or useless (default: warn).

complexity.description: Code that could be simpler (default: warn).

style.description: Code that does not follow conventions (default: warn).

pedantic.description: Lints that are often too strict (default: allow).

index-out-of-bounds.description: correctness: a constant index outside of an array of known length (`New Int[4]`, then `a[4]`).

unknown-state.description: suspicious: `GoToState("...")` with a state declared nowhere.

unchecked-cast.description: pedantic: the result of a cast between objects used without checking None.

unchecked-call-result.description: pedantic: the result of a function returning an object (which may always be None) used without checking None.

unused-local.description: suspicious: a local variable whose value is never read.

bool-literal-comparison.description: complexity: a comparison with True or False.

unknown-event.description: suspicious: an event spelled almost like one of the parents, probably a typo.

unknown-mod-callback.description: suspicious: RegisterForModEvent with a callback declared nowhere.

unknown-mod-event.description: suspicious: a custom event one typo away from another one, nothing connecting them.

unused-import.description: suspicious: an Import whose global functions are never called.

unused-script-variable.description: suspicious: a script variable whose value is never read.

repeating-update.description: suspicious: RegisterForUpdate, whose updates can pile up.

self-assignment.description: complexity: a variable assigned to itself.

redundant-cast.description: complexity: a cast to the type the value already has.

get-player-in-loop.description: pedantic: Game.GetPlayer() called in a loop.

format.description:
Formatter settings shared by the team. Unset values come from .editorconfig, then from the editor.

# Notes

Papyrus is case-insensitive, but Creation Kit may be case-sensitive in some contexts. Inconsistent casing between script names and their references (e.g. property types) may break existing Creation Kit bindings, such as UI bindings. Creation Kit's case-sensitivity in these contexts is undocumented.

workspace.description: Use [workspace.format] of the workspace, like in Cargo.toml. Without it, that table does not apply. Must be true, and alone in this table.

exclude.description: Scripts left as they are, e.g. ["src/vendor", "**/*_gen.psc"]. Relative to this file; `*` any text of a name, `?` one character, `**` any directories. Without `/` at any depth; a directory leaves out what is below it. Case is ignored.

keyword-case.description: Spelling of keywords. canonical is PascalCase with lowercase `as` and `extends`.

script-case.description: Spelling of script names: types, extends, Import, receivers like Debug.Trace. canonical is the ScriptName of the script (actor -> Actor). Only canonical or preserve: Creation Kit may lose the bindings of renamed scripts.

function-case.description: Spelling of functions and events. canonical is their declaration, or the one of the parent function they override (getvalue() -> GetValue()).

property-case.description: Spelling of properties. canonical is their declaration. Only canonical or preserve: Creation Kit may lose the bindings of renamed properties.

variable-case.description: Spelling of local variables, parameters and script variables. canonical is their declaration.

flag-case.description: Spelling of user flags. canonical is the flags file (hidden -> Hidden).

keywords.description: Spelling of single keywords, e.g. { as = "As" }. Only the case may change.

max-width.markdownDescription: Lines longer than this break with `\`, after commas and before `&&`, `||`; attributes alone on their line split into several (like `max_width` of rustfmt). `0`: keep lines as written.

max-blank-lines.description: Consecutive blank lines kept at most.

newline.description: Line break of formatted files; auto keeps the one of the file.

final-newline.description: End files with a line break.

workspace.description: Several projects in one folder, like Cargo workspaces. Like in Cargo.toml, nothing applies by itself: a member asks for each value with key.workspace = true, and for lints and format as a whole with workspace = true.

members.description: Member directories, each with a papyrus.toml; a trailing * means every subdirectory with one, e.g. "mods/*".

exclude.description: Directories matched by members that are not members.

var.description: Variables members may ask for with NAME.workspace = true. The paths of this file may use them.

path.description: Path of PapyrusCompiler.exe. Without it, the built-in compiler is used.

args.description: Extra arguments passed to the compiler as is.

compiler.description: Values members may ask for with key.workspace = true.

build.description: Values members may ask for with key.workspace = true.

imports.description: Other script source directories, in lookup order (after sources).

flags.description: The flags file, e.g. TESV_Papyrus_Flags.flg. Required by PapyrusCompiler.exe; without it, the built-in compiler uses the flags of Skyrim.

sources.markdownDescription: Directories of tests: `; #[test]` functions. Their scripts see the built-in `PapyrusAnalyzer` script (`PapyrusAnalyzer.AssertIntEq(...)`, or `Import PapyrusAnalyzer`). A test script extends the script it tests. Run by `papyrus_analyzer test`, never compiled into `output`.

dependencies.description: Projects whose sources this project imports (transitively), after its own sources: e.g. MCMHelper = { path = "../MCMHelper" }.

path.description: The directory of the project (with a papyrus.toml).

workspace.description: Take the value of the workspace, like in Cargo.toml.

nameCase.markdownDescription: `canonical`: as defined. `preserve`: as written. The other cases start from the definition. Names without known definition are kept.

boundNameCase.markdownDescription: `canonical`: as defined. `preserve`: as written. Names without known definition are kept. Script and property names are stored in the `.pex` and bound by Creation Kit, so they are never respelled otherwise.
